html:
Utendi wa Tambuka, "The Story of Tambuka", is an epic poem in the Swahili language, dated 1728. It is one of the oldest known Swahili manuscripts.

It was written by Bwana Mwengo wa Athman, reportedly at the court of the sultan of Pate, a town on the Swahili coast of today's Kenya. Its subject is the early Muslim war against the Byzantine emperor Heraclius, set around Tabuk in Arabia, and it tells of the courage and faith of the Prophet's companions in heroic verse. The poem has more than a thousand stanzas in the utendi metre, a four-line form still used in Swahili verse.

Like other early Swahili writing, it was written in Arabic script. It shows how the coastal towns had made Islamic stories their own and built a written literature in an African language long before colonial rule.
sum: Utendi wa Tambuka, "The Story of Tambuka", is an epic poem in the Swahili language, dated 1728. It is one of the oldest known Swahili manuscripts.
